title: Arbitrary-base-change and etale functoriality of a section Rees family
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $d\geq0$, and let $g:V\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type of pure relative dimension $d$, with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, $g s=1_S$.
For the ideal $\mathcal I$ of $s(S)$ set $\mathcal E=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$, $\pi:N_s=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\to S$, with zero section $z$. Set $D_sV=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]$, using the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$ generated by $t$ and the $b/t$, $b\in\mathcal I$. Its structural map is $q:D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_S$ and its section $\sigma$ is the augmentation $t\mapsto t$, $\mathcal I/t\mapsto0$, with coefficients restricted by $s$.
For every morphism $v:S'\to S$ of Noetherian schemes, put $V'=V\times_SS'$, with induced section $s'$ and ideal $\mathcal I'$. The canonical map
$$D_{s'}V'\longrightarrow D_sV\times_SS'$$
is an isomorphism, commuting with $t$, the augmented sections, the punctured trivializations, and the identifications of the pairs at $0$ and $1$. The conormal map $v^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$ and the induced normal-bundle map are isomorphisms. On a centred etale affine chart and an arbitrary affine base extension $R\to R'$, writing $B'=B\otimes_RR'$, $P'=R'[x]$, $I'=(x)B'$, the algebra identification is
$$B[t,I/t]\otimes_RR'\cong B'\otimes_{P'}R'[t,u]\cong B'[t,I'/t],$$
with $t\mapsto t$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, $x_j/t\mapsto x'_j/t$, and $[x_j]\mapsto[x'_j]$ on conormals. No flatness of $v$ is required. The new structural maps remain smooth separated of dimension $d$ and compactifiable.
If $h:V_1\to V$ is separated etale of finite type over $S$, $g_1=gh$ has a closed section $s_1$ with $h s_1=s$, and the square of centres is Cartesian, then
$$D_{s_1}V_1\cong D_sV\times_VV_1.$$
In particular its map to $D_sV$ is etale and preserves sections and both fibres. For an affine chart $B\to B_1$, with $I_1=IB_1$, its algebra map is $B_1\otimes_B B[t,I/t]\cong B_1[t,I_1/t]$. At zero its map is precisely the linear isomorphism of normal bundles induced by $[b]\mapsto[h^\sharp b]$ on conormals; at one it is $h$. All these canonical identifications agree on restrictions.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Local construction, explicit base-change maps and etale maps of pairs; old item Steps 5–6.

proof.text: First check the hypotheses after base change. The morphism $g':V'=V\times_SS'\to S'$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ by smooth base-change permanence, and separated of finite type by separated finite-type permanence. The square defining $s'$ is the pullback of $s$ along $V'\to V$, so $s'$ is closed, and $g's'=1_{S'}$ by the projections. Thus the centred-coordinate and Rees-geometry lemmas apply to $(g',s')$ over the given Noetherian $S'$.

source.place: Local construction; preservation of the section setting. Stacks 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Choose the affine centred charts of the centred-coordinate lemma, so $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to B$ is etale and $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)B$, with $B/I=R$ via the section. Cover the inverse images of their base opens in $S'$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R'$. Their fibre products with $\operatorname{Spec}B$ have rings $B'=B\otimes_RR'$ by the affine fibre-product lemma. Put $P'=R'[x_1,\ldots,x_d]=P\otimes_RR'$. The tensor universal property identifies $B'$ with $P'\otimes_PB$ as a $P'$-algebra, so the etale ring-base-change lemma, applied to the etale $P\to B$ and to $P\to P'$, shows that $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to\operatorname{Spec}P'$ is etale. The section quotient is $B'/IB'\cong R'$: maps out of this quotient are precisely maps out of $B$ and $R'$ agreeing on $R$ and annihilating $I$, by the tensor universal property. Consequently $I'=IB'=(x'_1,\ldots,x'_d)B'$, and these are again centred charts.

source.place: Local construction, centred etale charts; Stacks 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes).

proof.text: Apply the etale Rees-chart lemma to $P\to B$ and $P'\to B'$. Put $C=R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$, with $x_j$ acting as $tu_j$, and $C'=R'[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$ with the same rule. We obtain $B[t,I/t]\cong B\otimes_PC$ and $B'[t,I'/t]\cong B'\otimes_{P'}C'$. The tensor universal property gives $(B\otimes_PC)\otimes_RR'\cong (B\otimes_RR')\otimes_{P\otimes_RR'}(C\otimes_RR')$: both sides classify compatible ring maps out of $B,C,R'$, and the inverse maps on pure tensors are $((b\otimes c)\otimes r')\mapsto(b\otimes r')\otimes(c\otimes1)$ and $(b\otimes r')\otimes(c\otimes r'')\mapsto(b\otimes c)\otimes r'r''$. Identifying the polynomial coefficient extensions with $P'$ and $C'$ proves the displayed algebra isomorphism. It fixes $t$, sends $b$ to $b\otimes1$, and sends $x_j/t=u_j$ to $x'_j/t=u'_j$. No injection was tensored along $R\to R'$, so no flatness of that map is used.

source.place: Local construction, x_j=t u_j; explicit arbitrary-base-change calculation using the etale Rees presentation.

proof.text: The comparison is canonical before choosing coordinates: for a coefficient map $a:B\to B'$ carrying $I$ into $I'$, apply $a$ coefficientwise to Laurent polynomials; it restricts to $B[t,I/t]\to B'[t,I'/t]$, sending $t$ to $t$ and $b/t$ to $a(b)/t$. Multiplication with the $R'$-coefficients induces the comparison from $B[t,I/t]\otimes_RR'$. On centred charts this is exactly Step 3. After inverting $t$, it is the coefficientwise isomorphism $B[t,t^{-1}]\otimes_RR'\cong B'[t,t^{-1}]$; its inverse sends a coefficient $\sum b_i\otimes r'_i$ at degree $k$ to $\sum (b_it^k)\otimes r'_i$. The Rees-geometry lemma says centred deformation opens and the punctured deformation cover the entire family. Relative Spec identifies restrictions to these opens; the affine fibre-product lemma identifies their base changes with the tensors above. The Laurent formulas commute with further open restriction, so morphism gluing assembles the comparisons and their inverses. They give $D_{s'}V'\cong D_sV\times_SS'$ over both $V'$ and $\mathbf A^1_{S'}$.

source.place: Local construction and punctured trivialization; Stacks 01LX (lemma-spec-properties), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01JA (section-glueing-schemes).

proof.text: The augmentation is preserved: on a centred chart both composites send $t$ to $t$, every $u_j=x_j/t$ to zero, and $b$ to its section value, then extended to $R'$. These elements generate the chart algebra, so the composites agree. Setting $t=1$ sends $u_j$ to $x_j$ and the comparison becomes $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ on $B$; this is the required identification of the pair $(g',s')$ with the base-changed pair $(g,s)$. Inverting $t$ gives the punctured identification with exactly the same coefficient map by Step 4. Thus it preserves the sections and the specified punctured and one-fibre trivializations, not just the underlying spaces.

source.place: Local construction, augmented sections, x_j=t u_j, and the punctured and one-fibre identifications.

proof.text: On a centred chart the conormal has basis $[x_1],\ldots,[x_d]$ over $R$ by the centred-coordinate lemma. On the base-changed chart the classes $[x'_1],\ldots,[x'_d]$ generate $I'/I'^2$, since $I'=(x'_1,\ldots,x'_d)B'$ and $B'/I'=R'$ (Step 2). By the centred-coordinate lemma for $(g',s')$ (Step 1), $\mathcal E'$ is locally free of rank $d$, so $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ is covered by principal opens $D(f)$ with $(I'/I'^2)_f\cong R_f'^{\,d}$. Composing the surjection $R_f'^{\,d}\to(I'/I'^2)_f$, $e_j\mapsto[x'_j]$, with this isomorphism gives a surjective endomorphism of a finite module, bijective by the surjective-endomorphism lemma. So the surjection is injective on every $D(f)$, hence injective, and $[x'_1],\ldots,[x'_d]$ is a basis over $R'$. The canonical conormal map sends $[x_j]\otimes1$ to $[x'_j]$, so is an isomorphism, with the inverse specified on these bases. These are the intrinsic maps $[b]\mapsto[b\otimes1]$, hence they agree on restrictions and give $v^*\mathcal E\cong\mathcal E'$. A symmetric algebra map on these bases is the coefficient-extension polynomial isomorphism, so the induced normal bundle map is an isomorphism too. At zero the Rees-geometry lemma identifies a homogeneous class $[b]_m$ with $[bt^{-m}]$. The coefficient map takes this to $[(b\otimes1)t^{-m}]$, the image of $[b\otimes1]_m$ under the new zero-fibre identification. Since the symmetric-to-graded map is induced by products of degree-one classes, this is exactly the map induced by the conormal map, preserving the zero section. This proves the zero-fibre compatibility.

source.place: Local construction and normal-cone identification; Stacks 0633 (lemma-affine-conormal-sheaf), degree-one classes and their products.

proof.text: Apply the Rees-geometry lemma to $(g',s')$, whose hypotheses were checked in Step 1. It supplies smooth separated dimension-$d$ $q'$, the pair at zero $(\pi',z')$, Noetherian sources and compactifiability of $q'$ and $\pi'$, including the separated finite-type structural composites in its last clause. Since $\pi'$ is the fibre of $q'$ along $0:S'\to\mathbf A^1_{S'}$, smooth relative-dimension permanence and separated finite-type base-change permanence also give smooth separated dimension-$d$ $\pi'$. Thus the comparison identifies the base-changed structural maps with maps having the asserted geometry. This uses Noetherianity of $S'$ but no finite-type or flatness hypothesis on $S'\to S$.

source.place: Local construction, the new family and bundle have the same Noetherian smooth compactifiable geometry.

proof.text: Now take an affine restriction $B\to B_1$ of $h$. Since $h$ is etale it is flat, so the affine flatness criterion makes $B\to B_1$ a flat ring map, and the Cartesian square of centres gives $I_1=IB_1$. Tensor the inclusion $B[t,I/t]\hookrightarrow B[t,t^{-1}]$ with the flat $B$-module $B_1$; flat tensor exactness makes the resulting map injective. Coefficientwise multiplication identifies $B_1\otimes_BB[t,t^{-1}]$ with $B_1[t,t^{-1}]$: the inverse sends $\sum_k c_kt^k$ to $\sum_k c_k\otimes t^k$, and the tensor relations verify the two inverse identities. The image of $B_1\otimes_BB[t,I/t]$ in it is the $B_1$-subalgebra generated by $t$ and $b/t$ for $b\in I$. Indeed tensor elements are finite sums of scalar multiples of expressions in those generators. This equals $B_1[t,I_1/t]$: every $c\in I_1$ is a finite sum $\sum a_i b_i$, so $c/t=\sum a_i(b_i/t)$, and the reverse inclusion holds because $I$ maps into $I_1$. Thus the injective map has exactly the claimed image, giving $B_1\otimes_B B[t,I/t]\cong B_1[t,I_1/t]$.

source.place: Local construction, flat etale pullback of the Rees subalgebra; Stacks 00HD (lemma-flat), tensor injectivity. This is the explicit algebra argument, not a blow-up base-change assertion.

proof.text: Relative Spec, affine fibre products and morphism gluing assemble Step 8 into $D_{s_1}V_1\cong D_sV\times_VV_1$. Its map to $D_sV$ is the base change of the etale $h$ along $D_sV\to V$, hence etale by etale base-change stability. The augmentations agree on coefficients and send $b/t$ to zero; at one the coefficient map is $h$. For the zero fibre put $T=B/I$ and $T_1=B_1/I_1$. Flat tensor exactness and the tensor universal property give $T_1\otimes_T(I^m/I^{m+1})\cong I_1^m/I_1^{m+1}$, since $(IB_1)^m=I^mB_1$; the map sends $c\otimes[b]$ to $[c h^\sharp(b)]$. Products are preserved because both multiply representatives. In degree one this is the conormal pullback isomorphism. The affine centre map $\operatorname{Spec}T_1\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ is a restriction of the identity $S\to S$ under the Cartesian centres, so these local pullback maps identify the global conormal bundles over the same $S$. The centred-coordinate lemma identifies the original graded algebra with the symmetric algebra on this conormal. In its local bases this is a polynomial algebra; coefficient extension gives the symmetric algebra on the new conormal as well. Finally the general associated-graded Rees lemma identifies $[b]_m$ with $[bt^{-m}]$ on both zero fibres, without smoothness hypotheses. Hence the zero-fibre map is exactly the linear normal-bundle isomorphism induced by $[b]\mapsto[h^\sharp b]$, preserving its zero section.

source.place: Local construction, etale maps of pairs and the induced normal-bundle map; Stacks 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 0633 (lemma-affine-conormal-sheaf), 00HD (lemma-flat).

proof.text: Every comparison just constructed is induced by $t\mapsto t$ and $b/t\mapsto a(b)/t$, with coefficients mapped by $a$; a composite of coefficient maps gives the composite comparison on these generators. Restrictions are coefficient maps of this kind. The equalities therefore hold on each affine restriction and hence globally by morphism-gluing uniqueness. They include all stated section, punctured, zero- and one-fibre identifications. For $d=0$ the centred ideal is zero, its Rees algebra is $B[t]$, and the conormal is zero, so the same formulas apply with no $u_j$ or conormal basis vectors.

source.place: Local construction; compatibility on restrictions, compositions, and the empty coordinate sequence.

proof_origin.place: Local construction; explicit Rees algebra and generator calculations expanding the base-change and etale-map assertions, using Stacks 00HD, 01I4, 01LX, 02GO and 0633.
